correctness.rationale: An adjacent swap can create a 132 pattern only with both exchanged values. For an ascent x<y, legality means no earlier z<x; for a descent x>y, no later y<z<x. These necessary-and-sufficient criteria imply connectedness by inversion-increasing first ascents, a lower bound of two reversals of every pair below n plus n−1 crossings with n, and a constructive path of exactly (n−1)^2 moves. The maximum-element Catalan recurrence gives the edge generating function and coefficients. The independently executed all-vertex finite verifier confirms every n=2..10; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Pattern avoidance is a natural state constraint on adjacent-transposition sorting. The shortest path between two explicitly described permutations grows quadratically while the unconstrained distance grows linearly, giving unbounded geodesic distortion, with a constructive optimal route and forcing explanation. The all-parameter connectedness and exact edge enumeration characterize the ambient Catalan graph. This is a meaningful structural metric statement, not a routine count or arbitrary finite slice.
